name: Tall-Kneeling Medicine Ball Slam
definition: A bilateral self-start medicine-ball power slam performed upright on both knees and shins. The athlete raises a slam-safe low-bounce ball overhead, releases it forcefully into the clear floor directly in front, lets it settle, and resets. Partner-fed catches, half-kneeling support, standing slams, rotational floor targets, rebound catches, squat combinations, and retained-ball flexion remain outside this family.

variantAxes.description: How the ball reaches its release start.
Whether an external guide constrains the ball.

execution.startingPosition: Kneel upright on both knees and shins on a pad, hold a low-bounce medicine ball in both hands in front of the torso, and clear the slam area in front.
execution.movement: Raise the ball overhead without leaning backward, then drive it down and release it forcefully into the floor directly in front of the knees.
execution.endpoint: One repetition ends when the released ball strikes the floor in front of the knees.
execution.returnPhase: Let the ball settle, retrieve it safely, and reset upright with the ball at the torso before the next repetition.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep the ribs over the pelvis, the hips extended, and both knees grounded while the arms stay long through the slam.
execution.supportAndPosture: Use a padded kneeling surface, a low-bounce ball designed for repeated slams, and a clear slam-safe floor.
disqualifyingCompensations: Catching an overhead partner feed changes the exercise into a reactive slam.
Placing one foot forward changes the support to half-kneeling.
Arching backward to lift the ball removes the controlled trunk position.
